evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.text: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
If the target is a champion, they take increased damage for 4 seconds.
sources_quoted.role: Riot client text corroborates the debuff exists and lasts 4s, but carries no number.

sources_quoted.text: values [10.0, 100.0, 4.0, 8.0, 5.0, 1.5] with units [s, percent, s, percent, percent, flat]
sources_quoted.role: Independent parse of the same branch: the two candidate amp percents are exactly 8 and 5, in that textual order; no other percent appears.

sources_quoted.text: ... equal to {{as|{{rd|0 to 5 for 11|0 to 3.75 for 11|...}}|health}} ... [[Area of effect]], [[damage over time]], or [[damage|proc]] damage taken trigger this effect with the {{tip|ranged}} values.
sources_quoted.role: Control case pinning the {{rd|A|B}} template: B is explicitly named the ranged branch, so A is melee.
Control case: melee cleave 40% AD, ranged 20% AD — melee-first ordering.

sources_quoted.text: grant {{as|{{rd|{{fd|0.4}}%|{{fd|0.2}}%}} critical strike chance}} permanently, stacking up to {{rd|63|125}} times (capped at {{as|25% critical strike chance}})
sources_quoted.role: Control case: 0.4% x 63 = 25.2% (melee) and 0.2% x 125 = 25% (ranged) both hit the stated 25% cap only under melee-first ordering.
Control case: the second branch is literally the first x0.8 — the reduced ranged branch.

sources_quoted.text: post = raw · m(R) ⟺ raw = post · (1 + R/100)
sources_quoted.role: Confirms the engine models damage modifiers as multiplicative factors on the raw/post pipeline, so an 'increased damage taken' debuff is expressed as a multiplier (1 + p), not an additive term.

independent_computation.step_1_identify_effect: The leaf's own source string names 'Bloodsong — Expose Weakness'. Bloodsong is item id 3877 (data/items.json, data/item-atoms/3877.json). Its only passive, Spellblade, is the sole carrier of an 'Expose Weakness' debuff (S1). No other cached item or champion text in data/ defines an effect by that name (the only other mention is a Gangplank interaction note in data/champions.json: 'Bloodsong: Dealing damage with kegs to champions won't apply Expose Weakness to them.').
independent_computation.step_2_read_the_number: S1 states the debuffed champion takes '{{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources'. So the sourced amplification p is either 8% or 5% — there is no third admissible value, and S3's independent atom parse of the same branch yields exactly {8.0, 5.0} percent.
independent_computation.step_3_resolve_the_template: {{rd|A|B}} on the LoL wiki is the melee/ranged split, A = melee, B = ranged. Pinned by four independent control cases in the same cached file: C1 (B explicitly labelled the 'ranged values'), C2 (ranged cleave is the halved 20% AD), C3 (only melee-first makes both branches land on the stated 25% crit cap), C4 (B is literally A x 0.8). The split keys off the Bloodsong holder — the support who consumed Spellblade — not the ally whose damage is being amplified.
independent_computation.step_4_form_the_multiplier: 'Increased damage from all sources' is a damage-taken amplifier applied multiplicatively (C5): multiplier = 1 + p. Therefore melee Bloodsong holder -> 1 + 0.08 = 1.08; ranged Bloodsong holder -> 1 + 0.05 = 1.05. Rounding is exact, no level or stat scaling exists on this term (S3 shows no per-level unit), and the 4s duration / 1.5s cooldown affect only when the debuff is live, not its magnitude.
independent_computation.step_6_evaluate_old_value: The old state is <absent> — no support amplification recorded on this event, i.e. an effective multiplier of 1.0. 1.0 is not in the admissible set. Given the leaf is emitted at all with a Bloodsong holder in the roster and the debuff's own preconditions satisfied (Spellblade-empowered basic attack landing on a champion), the source text mandates a non-unit amplifier. Absence is unsupported by the cached wiki text.
independent_computation.step_7_evaluate_new_value: 1.08 is exactly the melee branch of {{rd|8%|5%}} under the template resolution pinned by C1-C4. It is a directly sourced, unrounded, admissible value, and its attached provenance string names the correct item and the correct debuff.
independent_computation.conclusion: 1.08 is correct for a melee Bloodsong holder; the only competing sourced value, 1.05, would be correct for a ranged holder. Between the two values actually under test, the new value is the one the source supports and the old (absent / 1.0) is not.

residual_uncertainty.statement: This oracle deliberately never read src/, tests/ or scripts/, so the roster composition of 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' — specifically whether the Bloodsong-holding support is a melee or a ranged champion — is not visible in the evidence tree. The scenario id does not appear anywhere under data/ (data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json contains 22 scenarios, none of them this one).
residual_uncertainty.impact: The verdict is stated for the pair actually under test and is robust: absence (1.0) is inadmissible under S1 either way. The one way 1.08 could still be wrong is if that scenario's Bloodsong holder is a ranged champion, in which case S1 mandates 1.05 instead.
residual_uncertainty.recommended_confirmation_by_a_reviewer_w: Check the attack-range class of the Bloodsong carrier in the cleaver_bloodsong_roster ally roster. Melee -> 1.08 stands. Ranged -> the leaf should read 1.05 and the melee/ranged branch selection is keying off the wrong participant (a plausible failure mode: reading the amp off the amplified attacker, e.g. the melee Black Cleaver holder, instead of off the Bloodsong holder).
